entities.title: Table-tennis scoring
entities.summary: A match is won by the first to 11 points, by two clear points.
entities.statement: The first side to 11 points wins, by two clear points. The serve changes every two points, and every point from 10–10.
acceptanceCriteria: 11–9 ends a match; 11–10 does not; 12–10 does.
From 10–10 the serve changes after every point.

origin.description: Rally's README, written for players and developers.

entities.title: Scores can't be faked
entities.summary: A score on the table is only ever what the server's replay of the match computed.
entities.statement: The server issues each one-player match's seed, replays the recorded match with the same engine before listing it, and accepts each seed once.
entities.rationale: A public table is only worth climbing if nobody can type a score into it.
acceptanceCriteria: A recording that does not play exactly one whole match is refused.
A recording made against another seed or level scores differently or not at all.

origin.description: Rally's README, written for players and developers.

entities.title: Friends play on their own devices
entities.summary: Two players can play each other online, each on their own computer, phone or tablet.
entities.statement: An online match started from the multiplayer page is played by two signed-in players on two devices, who see exactly the same match. There is no two-player game on one device.

origin.description: Rally's README, written for players and developers.

entities.title: Playing needs a sign-in
entities.summary: The game and its score API are for players signed in to icelander.net; the table stays public.
entities.statement: The game's page, a new match's seed and a score submission need a sign-in to icelander.net with the games:play role. The table, as JSON or as a page, needs none.

origin.description: The repository README: every game needs icelander.net's sign-in; the high-score tables stay public.

entities.title: Keys, touch or mouse
entities.summary: The paddle can be moved with the keyboard, a finger or the mouse.
entities.statement: W/S and the arrow keys move the paddle, and dragging or moving the mouse over the table sends it toward the pointer.

origin.description: Rally's README, written for players and developers.

entities.title: Only a name is stored
entities.summary: A score is stored with a name of up to 12 characters, and nothing else about the player.
entities.statement: The table stores a name of up to 12 plain characters with each score. No email address is asked for or stored; a signed-in player's address before the @ is only offered as a starting name.

origin.description: Rally's README, written for players and developers.

entities.title: An original game
entities.summary: Rally copies none of the paddle-and-ball games it follows: its name, look, sounds and code are its own.
entities.statement: Rally belongs to the paddle-and-ball genre but takes no name, artwork, sound or code from any game in it.

origin.description: Rally's README, written for players and developers.
